decision.summaryForCoordinator: v2 lands the v1 collision and the corpus holds up under byte-level checking. All ten catalogued fixtures exist, all ten digests reproduce by recomputation, all ten files are 0444, and the ten paths are distinct both exactly and under casefold — zero collision groups, against v1's ten members collapsing onto eight paths. Every declaredPermission matches its fixture's permissions[] token bytes exactly, including the leading-space, trailing-space, lowercased, capitalised and underscored variants where a byte-insensitive comparison would have hidden a defect. The closed set is set-equal to v9's seven live tokens, admit-all-seven carries exactly those seven with no non-member, and all nine refusal members are genuinely outside the set at expected PR-3, which v9 defines as token-outside-vocabulary. The four prototype strings are exactly the four v9's FX-1 names, and all four non-member categories v9 requires are present. The fixtures carry v11's typed-null reserved markers for updateData and stateMigration verbatim rather than populating them, and the permissions[] entries use v11's {permission, reason} shape. No decision-record bytes exist in any fixture, and the stated reason for that — that v9 names the record but never specifies its envelope — is true on live bytes, where 'envelope' occurs zero times. The predecessorV1 self-account is accurate on all three of its checkable claims. Custody is clean throughout: subject unmoved at 347fedd9 and 0444, four of four cited digests equal live bytes, file 08 pin equal to live and unmodified, HEAD 5d5d778, required-now 26, thirty gate rows, and neither QUALIFIED nor SATISFIED occurs anywhere in the subject. Seventeen attacks run, seventeen refuted, zero findings. Three observations are recorded, the first worth acting on: eight uncatalogued FX-2A fixture files now sit in the same pinned directory, written after this subject was frozen.
